title: Service exit 1067 can mean another launch mode of the same app already owns the port
symptoms: sc start reports 1067 ('process terminated unexpectedly') with no detail; repeated sc start does nothing
Looks like a permissions/install problem but isn't
explanation: If the same app can run as a manual process, an extension-spawned child, and a Windows service, an already-running instance holding the port makes the service's bind throw AddressInUseException → unhandled → exit 1067.
diagnosis: Get-WinEvent on the Application log — .NET's default handler logs the full exception (including port) even with no custom tracing. Then Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen to find and stop the PID holding the port.
